answer: Each agent’s identity seed is bound to a cryptographic proof that includes a unique ocean‑sized hash of its initial pigment‑derived token, stored on a verifiable bridge ledger. When an agent submits a request, the ledger checks that the token’s hash matches the seed; any mismatch aborts the operation, so a second identity cannot reuse the same token. Creating a fresh fake identity therefore requires locking up a new token and paying a staking fee of 0.5 % of the token’s market value per identity, plus a 24‑hour bonding period before activation.
